title: How HTTP works
idea: HTTP is the agreed language of the web: a client sends a request, the server sends back one response, and then they are done.

analogy.text: Ordering at a counter. You say what you want, the clerk hands over one answer, and the next order starts fresh.
analogy.breaks: A browser may send many orders at once on one connection.

points: A request has a method, a path, headers and an optional body.
A response has a status code, headers and an optional body.
HTTP is stateless: the server does not remember earlier requests.
HTTPS is the same conversation, encrypted with TLS.

messages.label: GET /books HTTP/1.1
messages.note: The browser sends a request line, then headers such as `Host` and `Accept`.

messages.label: run your code
messages.note: The server runs your code: routing, authentication, a database query.

messages.label: 200 OK + JSON body
messages.note: The server answers with a status line, headers and a body.

messages.label: use the response
messages.note: The browser uses the response. This exchange is over; the next request starts fresh.

code.title: A real exchange
code.caption: Node's `http` module: a server, one request to it, and what comes back.

pitfalls: Do not assume one request per connection; clients reuse connections.
A 200 status with an error message in the body confuses every client.
Plain HTTP exposes passwords and tokens; use HTTPS outside localhost.

options: The server forgets the client after each request
The server has no database or memory
The connection closes after every request
quiz.why: Each request must carry what the server needs. HTTP itself keeps nothing between requests.

takeaway: One request, one response, no memory in between.
